result.topic_en: Example I and its solution: the interpolating curve whose ordinates at abscissas nθ, (1−n)θ, (1+n)θ, … are ±f in pairs is put in finite form using the sine and tangent series summations, followed by corollaries giving functional relations for Δ = f:ω and a scholium linking the case to §25.

III. $\frac{1}{n+\omega}-\frac{1}{1-n-\omega}+\frac{1}{1+n+\omega}-\frac{1}{2-n-\omega}+\frac{1}{2+n+\omega}-\text{etc.}=\frac{\pi}{\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}$;
IV. $\frac{1}{n+\omega}+\frac{1}{1-n-\omega}-\frac{1}{1+n+\omega}-\frac{1}{2-n-\omega}+\frac{1}{2+n+\omega}+\text{etc.}=\frac{\pi}{\tang.(n+\omega)\pi}$.
His obseruatis euoluamus casus, quos harum summationum ope ad expressiones finitas reducere licet.

Exemplum I.

§. 40. Sint applicatae, quae abscissis $n\theta$, $(1-n)\theta$, $(1+n)\theta$, $(2-n)\theta$, $(2+n)\theta$ etc. respondent:
$p=f$; $q=f$; $r=-f$; $s=-f$; $t=+f$; $u=+f$; etc.
et per aequationem finitam relatio inter applicatam $y$ et abscissam $x=\theta\omega$ inuestigetur.

Solutio.

Corollarium primum pro hoc casu hanc praebet aequationem:
$\frac{\pi\Delta y}{f(n-\omega)}=+\frac{1}{n-\omega}-\frac{1}{1-n-\omega}-\frac{1}{1+n-\omega}+\frac{1}{2-n-\omega}+\frac{1}{2+n-\omega}-\text{etc.}$
$-\frac{1}{n+\omega}+\frac{1}{1-n+\omega}+\frac{1}{1+n+\omega}-\frac{1}{2-n+\omega}-\frac{1}{2+n+\omega}+\text{etc.}$
quae binae series reducuntur ope quatuor supra allatarum, quarum summatio constat, ad II–IV, ideoque aequatio quaesita in forma finita ita se habebit:
$\frac{\pi\Delta y}{f(n-\omega)}=\frac{\pi}{\sin.(n-\omega)\pi}-\frac{\pi}{\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}$,
quae expressio redigitur ad hanc:
$\frac{2\pi\cos.n\pi\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.(n-\omega)\pi.\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}=\frac{4\pi\cos.n\pi\sin.\omega\pi}{\cos.2\omega\pi-\cos.2n\pi}$ [?]
ita vt pro nostra curua haec habeatur aequatio:
$\frac{\pi\Delta y}{f(n-\omega)}=\frac{2\pi\cos.n\pi\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.(n-\omega)\pi\sin.(n+\omega)\pi}$.
Valorem ipsius $\Delta$ ante per formulas integrales expressum dedimus, cum autem ex superioribus sit $\Delta=\frac{1}{\pi(n+\omega)}$ [?], habebimus per productum infinitum:
$\Delta=\frac{1}{n+\omega}\cdot\frac{1(1-2n)}{(1-n)^2-\omega^2}\cdot\frac{2(1+2n)}{(1+n)^2-\omega^2}\cdot\frac{2(2-2n)}{(2-n)^2-\omega^2}\cdot\frac{3(2+2n)}{(2+n)^2-\omega^2}\cdot\text{etc.}$ [?]

vnde clarius constat, quam ex formulis integralibus, valorem $\Delta$ fieri infinitum, quoties fuerit $\omega=\pm(i\pm n)$, denotante $i$ numerum integrum quemcunque: euadem vero valorem $\Delta$ euanescere, casibus quibus est $n=\pm\frac{i}{2}$. Tum vero etiam notasse iuuabit, si abeunte $\omega$ in $1+\omega$ valor ipsius $\Delta$ notetur $\Delta'$, fore $\Delta'=-\frac{(1-n+\omega)\Delta}{n-\omega}$. Ac si simili modo $\Delta''$ conueniat valori $2+\omega$ loco $\omega$ assumto, erit
$\Delta''=\frac{-(2-n+\omega)\Delta'}{-(1-n+\omega)}=\frac{-(2-n+\omega)\Delta}{n-\omega}$.

Corollarium 1.

§. 41. Quatenus quantitas $\Delta$ ab $\omega$ pendet, consideretur vt eius functio, hocque modo designetur: $\Delta=f:\omega$; tum igitur erit
$f:(1+\omega)=\frac{n-1-\omega}{n-\omega}f:\omega$, et
$f:(2+\omega)=\frac{n-2-\omega}{n-\omega}f:\omega$ etc.
Quare si $\omega$ denotet numerum integrum quemcunque, habebitur hoc Theorema: $\frac{f:(i+\omega)}{n-i-\omega}=\frac{f:\omega}{n-\omega}$.

Corollarium 2.

§. 42. Cum deinde, sumto $\omega$ negatiuo, fit
$f:(-\omega)=\frac{n+\omega}{n-\omega}f:\omega$, erit $\frac{f:(-\omega)}{n+\omega}=\frac{f:\omega}{n-\omega}$,
hinc etiam in genere $\frac{f:(i-\omega)}{n-i+\omega}=\frac{f:\omega}{n-\omega}$.

Scholion.

§. 43. Hic casus respondet illi, quem supra §. 25. euoluimus, vbi applicatae datae quoque erant abscissarum sinus; ac pro praesenti quidem casu statui oportet $\theta=\pi$,

items.english: Let the ordinates corresponding to the abscissas nθ, (1−n)θ, (1+n)θ, (2−n)θ, (2+n)θ etc. be p=f, q=f, r=−f, s=−f, t=+f, u=+f, etc., and let the relation between the ordinate y and the abscissa x=θω be found by a finite equation.

items.quote: Quare si $\omega$ denotet numerum integrum quemcunque, habebitur hoc Theorema: $\frac{f:(i+\omega)}{n-i-\omega}=\frac{f:\omega}{n-\omega}$.
items.english: Therefore, if ω [i] denotes any integer, this theorem holds: f(i+ω)/(n−i−ω) = f(ω)/(n−ω).
Hence also in general f(i−ω)/(n−i+ω) = f(ω)/(n−ω).
